title: Quick Autism Test
summary: Ten personal questions about communication, routines, sensory differences and masking.

landing.intro: Have you always experienced social situations, routines or sensory input differently? These 10 quick questions look at traits adults often overlook.

about.body:
This ten-question self-check asks about social communication, literal language, routines, focused interests, repetitive movement, sensory differences and masking. It groups your answers into a descriptive trait summary; it does not calculate whether you are autistic.

Autism is a lifelong form of neurodivergence, not an illness. Autistic people are diverse, and individual traits can overlap with ADHD, anxiety and many other experiences. A proper assessment considers development from childhood, current life and more than a short online questionnaire.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
steps: Choose the answer that best reflects your usual experience.
Think across different settings and earlier stages of life where possible.
Reveal your personal trait summary after all ten questions.

about.disclaimer: For general information only. This is not a diagnostic test, validated autism screener or substitute for a professional assessment. It cannot confirm or rule out autism, ADHD or another condition. If these traits affect daily life or you want to understand them better, speak with a qualified professional familiar with adult autism.

stage-1.preAdCopy: Your ten answers have been reviewed and your personal trait summary is ready to reveal.

profile-1.title: No Single Pattern Dominated
profile-1.copy: Your answers did not highlight one dominant group of traits. That cannot rule out autism, and some people adapt or mask in ways a short self-check cannot capture. Professional advice is appropriate if you still have questions or need support.

profile-2.title: Social Cues May Take Extra Work
profile-2.copy: Your answers centred on conversation, implied meaning, facial expression or the effort of navigating social situations. These experiences can have many explanations. A qualified professional can explore the wider pattern and your developmental history.

profile-3.tier: SENSORY OR ROUTINE TRAITS STOOD OUT
profile-3.title: Predictability May Matter More Than People Realise
profile-3.copy: Your answers highlighted sensory differences, focused interests, repetitive movement or a strong preference for routine. These traits are not inherently negative, but support or adjustments may help when they cause stress or exhaustion.

profile-4.tier: MASKING OR SUPPORT NEEDS STOOD OUT
profile-4.title: The Hidden Effort May Be Significant
profile-4.copy: Your answers suggest that adapting, masking or recovering from everyday demands may take substantial effort. This result is not a diagnosis, but it may be worth discussing an adult autism assessment or practical support with a qualified professional.

autism-q1.question: How easy is it to work out what someone means from their tone, face or gestures?
answers: Usually straightforward
I sometimes need extra context
I often have to work it out consciously
It regularly causes confusion or exhaustion

autism-q2.question: How do you respond to hints, sarcasm or expressions that are not meant literally?
answers: I usually understand them easily
I occasionally take them literally
I often prefer direct, precise wording
I frequently miss them or learn the meaning later

autism-q3.question: What are unstructured conversations or small talk like for you?
answers: Mostly natural
I sometimes rehearse what to say
I consciously follow learned social rules
They can be exhausting or difficult to navigate

autism-q4.question: How strongly do sounds, lights, smells, textures or crowded places affect you?
answers: About as expected
Some sensations bother me noticeably
I seek or avoid particular sensations
Sensory input can overwhelm me or limit activities

autism-q5.question: How do unexpected changes to plans or routines usually feel?
answers: I adapt fairly easily
They can unsettle me
I rely on preparation or familiar routines
They can cause significant distress or derail my day

autism-q6.question: How do you engage with subjects or activities that interest you?
answers: I enjoy them casually
I can become deeply absorbed
I learn or talk about them in exceptional detail
They can dominate my attention or help me recover

autism-q7.question: Do repetitive movements, sounds or routines help you regulate how you feel?
answers: Rarely
Sometimes, often without noticing
Yes, they help me focus or settle
I rely on them during stress or sensory overload

autism-q8.question: How much do you change or monitor your behaviour to fit into social situations?
answers: Very little
I occasionally copy or rehearse
I regularly monitor my expressions and responses
I mask heavily and feel exhausted afterwards

autism-q9.question: After busy social or sensory situations, what do you usually need?
answers: No unusual recovery
Some quiet time
A familiar routine or extended time alone
Substantial recovery time because I feel overloaded

autism-q10.question: Which statement best describes these traits across your life?
answers: They are occasional and have little effect
Mostly social differences have been longstanding
Mostly sensory or routine differences have been longstanding
Several traits began early and affect more than one area of life
